- What we need from you: a representative prompt set and a short list of edge cases (examples that should be redacted or require conservative answers).
- What we'll deliver: recommended model variants, benchmark links, and an initial evaluation run on your prompts. We'll flag potential quality regressions and redaction failure modes.

I've looped in Aditya (SE) and Dev (solutions) — they'll share model recommendations and the benchmark link.

Thanks — talk soon.

Thanks Jordan — got the CSV and PII mapping. A quick set of recommendations and links: 

- Recommended models (initial):
  - redwood-chat-7b-q4f16: low-latency, good for majority of FAQ traffic, cost-effective.
  - redwood-chat-13b-hetro: higher capab for multi-step policy reasoning; use for critical-policy routes where precision matters.
  - redwood-instruct-3b-int8: for short completions where hallucination risk is lower and throughput matters.

- Benchmarks: run your prompt set through our internal chat-qa benchmark (https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/chat-qa-2026). It will output per-prompt accuracy, calibration, and hallucination flags.

- Redaction guidance: we recommend a two-step approach — client-side redaction where possible + server-side detection for edge cases. For logs, we can enable automatic token-level redaction for fields matching your PII map; we'll need a canonical field list from you (looks like acme_pii_map.xlsx covers most).

- Evaluation plan: we'll run the 50 prompts plus the edge cases on the 7b and 13b variants, return per-example outputs and a regression report. Expected turnaround: 48 hours after you confirm delivery method.

Action items:
- Jordan: confirm Drive vs HubSpot upload for the prompt CSV (either works for us).
- Priya: can you confirm if Acme requires hashed storage or fully redacted logs for evaluation? That will affect whether we run evals in-hosted mode or a private deployment.

I'll kick off the benchmark as soon as we have confirmation.

—Aditya
